scenes.title: A Form for an Empty Building
scenes.narration: Dalia arrived to inspect a boarding house that had been closed for years. Her agency wanted a simple statement that its six rooms were empty. She carried the survey in a blue envelope and a brass key on a yellow tag. Inside, a black guest ledger lay on the reception desk. Dust covered the counter around it, but not the book. She put down her envelope without opening the ledger. First, she would check the rooms.
scenes.prompt: What made the ledger stand out from its surroundings?

options.text: It had no dust while the counter around it did
It was the only object mentioned on the survey form
It had been locked inside one of the six rooms

scenes.explanation: The book is clean even though dust covers the counter around it. That difference catches Dalia's attention.

scenes.title: Six Doors, Six Names
scenes.narration: Dalia checked all six rooms. The beds were bare, the cupboards open, and no personal belongings remained. Back at reception, she opened the ledger. Six names filled the current page, each followed by the word "present." She checked the dates against her survey: they were today's. Perhaps someone had recently used the building. Yet the rooms had contained none of the small signs of ordinary life. She left the ledger open while writing down what she had actually observed.
scenes.prompt: Why did Dalia hesitate to accept the ledger as proof of residents?

options.text: The ledger listed fewer rooms than the building had
The rooms contained no signs of ordinary life
Her agency had forbidden her to inspect the cupboards

scenes.explanation: The ledger lists current guests, but the empty rooms do not support that account.

scenes.title: A Place Already Written
scenes.narration: When Dalia looked up from the survey, one entry had changed. Her own full name now occupied the last line of the guest ledger. The handwriting resembled hers, although her pen had touched only the survey. The yellow-tag key was still beside the blue envelope. Both the front door and courtyard exit were open. She could take the book to her agency or leave it behind. Either way, she would not sign a claim that she could no longer support.
scenes.prompt: What had Dalia decided before choosing what to take?

options.text: To sign the guest ledger as a new resident
To lock both exits and inspect the rooms again
Not to certify a claim she could not support

scenes.explanation: Dalia says she will not sign a claim she can no longer support, before deciding whether to take the book.

transitions.label: Take the ledger to the agency as evidence
Leave the ledger and submit only the survey

scenes.title: A Book beyond the Gate
scenes.narration: Dalia placed the ledger and survey envelope under her arm, took the key, and walked through the front door. Outside the gate, every page of the ledger was blank. At the agency, she showed the book to a colleague and described the six names and her own. He recorded her account without asking her to return alone. The inspection remained incomplete. For Dalia, leaving a form unfinished felt less frightening than pretending she had understood the building.
scenes.prompt: Why did Dalia leave the inspection incomplete?

options.text: She could not honestly explain or certify what she had found
She had forgotten to bring the survey envelope
Her colleague asked her to sign the blank guest pages

scenes.explanation: Dalia cannot honestly explain the conflicting evidence, so she does not certify the inspection.

scenes.title: An Address She Did Not Accept
scenes.narration: Dalia left the guest ledger open and took only her survey envelope and key. At the courtyard gate, she checked the form: it still contained her careful notes, not a list of residents. She submitted a report marked "occupancy unverified" and declined another visit without a colleague. At home, she put the yellow-tag key in the agency return box. Whatever the ledger had called her, she had chosen not to make its address her own.

Her survey envelope and key, but not the ledger
Only a blank form from the reception desk

scenes.explanation: She leaves the ledger inside and takes her own survey envelope and key through the courtyard exit.

visualContinuity.characters: Dalia, a 49-year-old woman with a narrow face, light brown skin, deep-set brown eyes, straight dark hair cut at the jaw, a worn olive coat, grey sweater, black trousers and brown boots.
visualContinuity.locations: A shuttered six-room boarding house: front reception desk with a black guest ledger, a straight corridor with six numbered doors, a courtyard exit at the far end, and an outside street gate. A blue survey envelope and a yellow-tag key belong to the inspection kit.
visualContinuity.clues: Dalia brings a blue survey envelope and a brass key on a yellow tag. A black ledger remains at reception until the carry-book route. Six rooms appear empty; the ledger first lists six guests and later Dalia's full name. The blue survey form is distinct from the guest ledger.

authoringNotes.learningFocus: Contraste entre observação e registro, inferências cautelosas e escolha diante de evidência incerta.
authoringNotes.proposedAudience: Adultos aprendendo inglês; sem violência gráfica. Faixa etária não é um recurso implementado no site.
authoringNotes.reviewStatus: Produção e envio à VPS concluídos: WAVs gerados a partir do texto exato e conferidos por transcrição automática; artes 2D dark inspecionadas e corrigidas por cena. Grafo e questões verificados pelos testes. Não declara revisão auditiva humana nem certificação CEFR.
authoringNotes.supportedGameplay: Cenas, narração pré-gravada, uma pergunta por cena, uma bifurcação e dois finais. Objetos, tecnologias e ações são elementos da ficção; não requerem inventário, fala do jogador, combate ou novos eventos de gameplay.
authoringNotes.levelNote: Nível e tamanho são propostas editoriais, não certificação automática CEFR.
humanReviewChecklist: Revisar compreensão e naturalidade do inglês no nível indicado.
Revisar se cada pergunta tem exatamente uma resposta apoiada no texto.
Revisar continuidade, motivação, tom e ambos os finais.
Revisar o registro de autoria e autorização do texto; preencher créditos e evidências das mídias que forem produzidas.
Produzir e escutar WAVs a partir de audioText; revisar e produzir as imagens-base e loops.
Importar como rascunho, validar mídia no servidor e publicar somente após revisão.
